recognize_zh: 骨髓切片 CD163 免疫染色中，大量大型上皮樣細胞的細胞膜與細胞質呈強烈棕色顆粒狀、樹枝狀陽性，勾勒出細胞輪廓，支持這群上皮樣細胞為組織球（histiocyte／macrophage）來源。
features: Dense sheet-like infiltrate of large cells with ovoid pale nuclei replacing much of the marrow
Strong CD163 staining with membranous and coarse granular cytoplasmic pattern
Positive cells show irregular, dendritic-like cytoplasmic extensions outlining cell borders
describe_en: CD163 immunohistochemistry on the bone marrow core biopsy shows strong membranous and granular cytoplasmic staining in numerous large epithelioid cells, which form a dense, sheet-like infiltrate with irregular cytoplasmic processes. Interspersed smaller hematopoietic cells are negative. In conjunction with CD34 negativity and only dot-like keratin staining, the CD163 expression supports histiocytic/monocyte-macrophage lineage of the epithelioid infiltrate; distinction between a reactive histiocytic proliferation and a histiocytic neoplasm requires correlation with cytologic atypia, extent, and additional markers.

ddx.vs: Carcinoma cells are CD163-negative with strong diffuse cytokeratin, whereas these cells are CD163-positive with only dot-like keratin.
Histiocytic sarcoma is also CD163-positive but shows marked cytologic atypia and mitoses on H&E with CD68/lysozyme, and requires exclusion of other lineages.
Monoblasts/promonocytes are smaller with fine chromatin, often CD34/CD117 variable, and typically CD163 weak to negative, with blasts evident on aspirate.
Resident macrophages are scattered, interstitial, and dendritic rather than forming a dense cohesive sheet of large epithelioid cells.
